es: Presentar y defender una postura oral de un minuto con introducción, dos argumentos, una hipótesis, una concesión y un cierre.

teaching.en: My topic today is whether schools should start later.
teaching.es: Mi tema de hoy es si los colegios deberían empezar más tarde.
teaching.explanationEs: Una buena introducción dice el tema en una frase: My topic today is…
teaching.audioText: My topic today is whether schools should start later.

teaching.en: Firstly, teenagers need more sleep, and studies show that tired students learn less.
teaching.es: En primer lugar, los adolescentes necesitan dormir más, y los estudios muestran que los estudiantes cansados aprenden menos.
teaching.explanationEs: El primer argumento lleva firstly y una prueba que lo sostiene.
segments: Firstly, teenagers need more sleep, and studies
show that tired students learn less.
teaching.audioText: Firstly, teenagers need more sleep, and studies show that tired students learn less.

teaching.en: Secondly, a later start would reduce the stress of the morning rush.
teaching.es: En segundo lugar, empezar más tarde reduciría el estrés de las prisas de la mañana.
teaching.explanationEs: Secondly abre el segundo argumento; would + verbo base habla de un efecto posible.
segments: Secondly, a later start would reduce
the stress of the morning rush.
teaching.audioText: Secondly, a later start would reduce the stress of the morning rush.

teaching.en: Suppose schools started at nine; I think students would be calmer.
teaching.es: Supongamos que los colegios empezaran a las nueve; creo que los estudiantes estarían más tranquilos.
teaching.explanationEs: La hipótesis usa suppose + pasado simple y would + verbo base.
segments: Suppose schools started at nine; I
teaching.audioText: Suppose schools started at nine; I think students would be calmer.

teaching.en: Admittedly, some parents would have to change their schedules.
teaching.es: Es cierto que algunos padres tendrían que cambiar sus horarios.
teaching.explanationEs: La concesión reconoce un punto contrario, sin abandonar la postura.
teaching.audioText: Admittedly, some parents would have to change their schedules.

teaching.en: In short, a later start is a small change with a big benefit.
teaching.es: En resumen, empezar más tarde es un cambio pequeño con un gran beneficio.
teaching.explanationEs: El cierre repite tu postura en una frase corta: In short, …
segments: In short, a later start is a
small change with a big benefit.
teaching.audioText: In short, a later start is a small change with a big benefit.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál de estas frases plantea una hipótesis?

choices.text: Suppose classes began at nine; students would be calmer.
Classes start at eight and students are tired.
Classes will start at nine next year.

feedback.es: Suppose + pasado simple y would + verbo base plantean una situación imaginada. Las otras dos describen hechos.

hint.es: La hipótesis combina suppose con would.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con el bloque de la intervención que cumple.

pairs: My topic today is bike lanes.
Firstly, it saves money. Secondly, it helps the town.
In short, bike lanes are worth it.

feedback.es: Cada frase tiene un papel: abrir el tema, dar razones, conceder un punto o cerrar.

pairs: My topic today is bike lanes.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frases reconocen un punto del otro lado y vuelven a tu postura?

choices.text: Firstly, it would cost more. Secondly, the benefit is bigger.
Admittedly, it would cost more. However, the benefit is bigger.
In short, it would cost more. Suppose the benefit is bigger.

feedback.es: Admittedly reconoce el coste y However vuelve a la postura. Las otras dos secuencias no hacen ninguna concesión.

origin.text: Quieres reconocer un punto del otro lado antes de volver a tu postura.

prompt.es: Escribe tu cierre con in short.

answer.text: In short, public transport is a small change with a big benefit.
accepted: In short, public transport is a small change with a big benefit.
In conclusion, public transport is a small change with a big benefit.
To sum up, public transport is a small change with a big benefit.
In short, using public transport is a small change with a big benefit.

feedback.es: El cierre repite tu postura en una frase breve: In short, + la idea principal.

origin.text: Tu cierre: usar el transporte público es un cambio pequeño con un gran beneficio.

My topic today is whether phones should be allowed in class.

feedback.es: My topic today is whether… anuncia el tema y, después de whether, el sujeto va antes de should. Las otras dos tienen el orden de palabras o la preposición mal.

prompt.es: Escribe el guion de tu intervención con los datos dados, de 50 a 110 palabras.

answer.text: My topic today is whether schools should have a daily reading hour. Firstly, reading improves vocabulary. Secondly, it reduces stress. Suppose every student read for twenty minutes; I think they would get better marks. Admittedly, some students prefer other activities. However, the benefit is bigger. In short, a daily reading hour is a small change with a big benefit.
accepted: My topic today is whether schools should have a daily reading hour. Firstly, reading improves vocabulary. Secondly, it reduces stress. Suppose every student read for twenty minutes; I think they would get better marks. Admittedly, some students prefer other activities. However, the benefit is bigger. In short, a daily reading hour is a small change with a big benefit.

Today I'd like to talk about a daily reading hour at school. First, reading improves vocabulary. Second, it reduces stress. If every student read for twenty minutes, I think they would get better marks. Admittedly, some students prefer other activities. However, the benefit is bigger. To sum up, it is a small change with a big benefit.

feedback.es: El guion tiene introducción, dos argumentos, una hipótesis, una concesión y un cierre, cada bloque con su estructura.

origin.text: Tema: los colegios deberían tener una hora de lectura diaria. Argumentos: mejora el vocabulario; reduce el estrés. Hipótesis: si todos leyeran veinte minutos, sacarían mejores notas. Concesión: algunos alumnos prefieren otras actividades. Cierre: es un cambio pequeño con gran beneficio.
